In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence for oxidative damage to alpha 2-PI in the lung is not compelling.
cigarette smoke, in addition to causing lung damage, also impairs alpha 1-antiproteinases in the lower respiratory tracts of smokers.

cigarette smoke does not cause emphysema by damaging alpha 1-antiproteinases, although it is possible that cigarette smoke and/or inflammatory cells damage alpha 1- antiproteinases in some patients with emphysemas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cigarette smoke and phlogistic stimuli damage alpha 1- PI, and the damaged enzyme is less effective in protecting elastin from neutrophil elastases.
the pathogenesis of cigarette smoke-induced emphysema involves oxidative damage to alpha 2-PI.
cigarette smoking is a risk factor for developing emphysema and that damage to alpha 0-PI in the lungs may be one of the mechanisms by which cigarette smoke causes this disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alpha 1- PI in lung lavage fluid is oxidatively damaged in emphysema and that this damage is associated with reduced elastase inhibitory activity.
the oxidative modification of alpha 1- PI is an important mechanism of inactivation in vivo and that the oxidative modification is associated with loss of elastase inhibition.
alpha 1- PI is not a major target for oxidative damage in vivo.
